title: Remove or enforce the calendar account read_only capability
description:
## Finding

`CalendarAccount::read_only` is a public, serialized option but no production path reads it. Setting `read_only = false` does not enable writes, change backend capabilities, or alter any host behavior.

The service declares create/update/delete methods and capability bits, yet its module contract says every built-in is read-only and all optional write methods default to `Unsupported`. The config field is described as 'belt-and-braces,' but an unenforced capability switch is misleading API surface and creates a future fail-open hazard if a backend later gains writes without a single authorization gate.

## Evidence at audited commit

* `crates/thegn-core/src/config_calendar.rs:254-256,288-307`: public serialized `read_only` field, default true.
* `config/config.toml.example:397`: example exposes the setting.
* Repository-wide production search finds no calendar read of the field.
* `crates/thegn-svc/src/calendar/mod.rs:1-14,110-145`: write methods exist but every built-in inherits `Unsupported`.
* `crates/thegn-core/src/config_calendar_tests.rs:383`: tests cover only the default value, not enforcement.

## Impact

Configuration and generated API documentation imply a capability that cannot be enabled today. More seriously, future write support could accidentally ignore a user/account read-only boundary because no centralized enforcement seam exists.

## Required implementation

* For the current read-only product, remove the option from the public schema/example and warn on obsolete configured values; or implement a single fail-closed authorization gate used by every create/update/delete route before provider/plugin invocation.
* Derive advertised `CalendarCaps` from both provider support and account policy. `read_only = true` must force every write capability false and every direct write call to a typed denial.
* Do not rely on UI hiding or plugin self-report. Enforce at the router/host boundary and audit denied attempts.
* Make command-plugin negotiation truthful: a plugin cannot gain calendar mutation authority beyond account policy.
* Add a consumed-config-field ratchet so serialized capability/security settings cannot remain dead.

## Verification

Test all three mutation verbs through router, direct backend adapters, and command-plugin paths with read-only true/false and contradictory provider capabilities. Test schema migration and diagnostics for removed/obsolete fields if the option is deleted.

## Dependencies

Dependency-ready. Coordinate plugin capability truthfulness with THE-166 and public plugin verb coverage with THE-162.
